Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. - **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.

- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`
# lines below, which converge nightly — this file does not, so it must not grow
# logic. This copy is hand-maintained — the canon has no converge — so it is
# edited in the same commit as the stub beside it.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      continuation_depth:
        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A backstop against a wedged runner, well clear of any declared
    # `code_work_timeout`; the heartbeat's leash is what bounds real work.
    timeout-minutes: 350
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:

### Executing a task with secrets — the whole path

GitHub Actions secrets are the only secret store in the system, and the
executor workflow is the only consumer. End to end:

1. **Declaration** — `task.mjs` lists `required_secrets: ['CHROME_STORE_TOKEN']`:
   names only. The declaration is vendored to every consuming repo verbatim,
   which is exactly why it must never hold more than a name.
2. **Storage** — values live as repo Actions secrets, set once by the owner
   in repo settings. Nothing else in the system stores, copies, or logs them.
3. **Wiring** — the wiring converge stamps each declared name into the
   **executor workflow's env** (`CHROME_STORE_TOKEN:
   ${{ secrets.CHROME_STORE_TOKEN }}`). The scheduler run and the janitor workflows
   get no secrets — they never execute task code.
4. **Execution** — after claim and a go verdict, the executor runs the work step as
   a subprocess (task dir cwd, timeout) whose env carries exactly the
   declared names. **The work step is the only task code that ever sees values.**
5. **The agent hop carries nothing** — the hand-off writes body sections and
   calls the invocation endpoint with a prompt naming the issue and nonce;
   the session works under its own identity. A task whose agent phase needs
   a privileged effect routes it through the work step's delivered artifact or a
   wider invocation endpoint — never a secret in the session.
6. **Endpoint tokens ride the same rail** (§12): config maps endpoint name →
   URL + the *name* of the Actions secret; the stamp puts it in the executor
   env; the executor reads it only at the moment of the API call. The CCR
   session-creation token is simply the default endpoint's entry.
7. **Missing secret** — declared but not configured: baselining asks the
   owner on its standing issue (the adoption-interview posture), and until
   set, execution parks the affected item `needs-human` +
   `task:status:needs-human-action` naming the missing secret — at the work step for `required_secrets`, at hand-off for an
   endpoint token. Nothing fails silently; the task just doesn't work yet.
8. **Rotation** — rotate the value in repo settings; nothing else changes,
   because names are the interface everywhere above.

Steps 2–3 and 6–8's storage half are Actions-platform behavior the simulator
deliberately does not model (prose rows in the coverage map); the
needs-human convergence postures are ordinary sim territory.

1. **Declaration** — `task.mjs` lists `required_secrets: ['CHROME_STORE_TOKEN']`:
   names only. The declaration is vendored to every consuming repo verbatim,
   which is exactly why it must never hold more than a name.
2. **Storage** — values live as repo Actions secrets, set once by the owner
   in repo settings. Nothing else in the system stores, copies, or logs them.
3. **Wiring** — the wiring converge stamps each declared name into the
   **executor workflow's env** (`CHROME_STORE_TOKEN:
   ${{ secrets.CHROME_STORE_TOKEN }}`). The scheduler run and the janitor workflows
   get no secrets — they never execute task code.
4. **Execution** — after claim and a go verdict, the executor runs the work step as
   a subprocess (task dir cwd, timeout) whose env carries exactly the
   declared names. **The work step is the only task code that ever sees values.**
5. **The agent hop carries nothing** — the hand-off writes body sections and
   calls the invocation endpoint with a prompt naming the issue and nonce;
   the session works under its own identity. A task whose agent phase needs
   a privileged effect routes it through the work step's delivered artifact or a
   wider invocation endpoint — never a secret in the session.
6. **Endpoint tokens ride the same rail** (§12): config maps endpoint name →
   URL + the *name* of the Actions secret; the stamp puts it in the executor
   env; the executor reads it only at the moment of the API call. The CCR
   session-creation token is simply the default endpoint's entry.
7. **Missing secret** — declared but not configured: baselining asks the
   owner on its standing issue (the adoption-interview posture), and until
   set, execution parks the affected item `needs-human` +
   `task:status:needs-human-action` naming the missing secret — at the work step for `required_secrets`, at hand-off for an
   endpoint token. Nothing fails silently; the task just doesn't work yet.
8. **Rotation** — rotate the value in repo settings; nothing else changes,
   because names are the interface everywhere above.

Steps 2–3 and 6–8's storage half are Actions-platform behavior the simulator
deliberately does not model (prose rows in the coverage map); the
needs-human convergence postures are ordinary sim territory.

content.text:
## Is naming required?

**Yes, for the form the executor uses.** GitHub gives no "export all secrets as env vars" primitive — the `secrets` context is only reachable through an expression, and each one has to be interpolated somewhere. The two things that look like "pass all" don't remove the naming:

- **`secrets: inherit`** works only on a *reusable-workflow call* (`jobs.<id>.uses:`). It makes the caller's secrets resolvable in the callee's `secrets` context — the callee still names each one in its own `env:`. This repo already demonstrates that shape: `chrome-extension-release.yml:120` passes `secrets: inherit`, and `chrome-extension-publish-store.yml:57-61` still spells out all four `CHROME_*` names.
- **`${{ toJSON(secrets) }}`** genuinely does expand the whole context into one variable. It is the only true "pass all", and I'd argue against it here:
  - `required_secrets` is currently more than wiring — it's the audit surface *and* the diagnosis (`missingSecrets`, `code-work-run.mjs:25`, which is what parks an item `needs-human-action` naming the one missing secret). A blob keeps the declarations anyway, so you buy nothing and lose the "the executor's env is exactly the declared set" property.
  - Masking is registered per exact literal. Inside JSON a secret containing `"`, `\` or a newline appears **escaped**, no longer matching the registered mask — so `toJSON(secrets)` is a known way to print a secret unmasked.
  - It would also drag every *unrelated* repo secret (the Chrome store credentials) into the executor job.

The hand-maintained list is 3 lines and regenerated on members from the `# claudinite:secrets` marker (`converge-wiring.mjs:105-117`). I'd keep it.

⚠️ I could not verify the platform behaviour against docs.github.com in this session — the egress proxy blocks that domain outright (`EGRESS_BLOCKED`), and per the pack rule I didn't work down alternate sources for the same fact. The claims above are from knowledge plus the in-repo corroboration cited; the `toJSON` masking caveat in particular is worth one confirmation from an unblocked environment.

## Are they visible in transit?

- **In the workflow file** — names only. `${{ secrets.X }}` never renders a value into the committed text, which is why `convergeExecutorWorkflow` can safely write this file.
- **In the Actions log** — each value used in the job is registered for masking and renders `***`. The runner does not itself echo `env:` values. Caveat: masking is exact-literal, so a *transformed* value (base64'd, split across lines, JSON-escaped, substring) is not masked.
- **Trigger surface** — the executor fires only on `issues: labeled` and `workflow_dispatch`. No `pull_request_target`, so there's no fork-PR path to these secrets. Clean.
- **The agent hop** — confirmed carrying nothing: `invoke.mjs` sends one freeform `text` field with item number + nonce, and the endpoint token is read only at the moment of the call. The session itself holds no secret.

## Two things that don't hold up

**1. Every task's code-work gets every stamped secret.** `code-work-run.mjs:67` builds the child env as `{ ...env, ...codeWorkEnv(...) }`, where `env` defaults to the executor's whole `process.env` (`executor.mjs:629` passes no `env`). So all three stamped secrets reach the work step of *every* task — including the ~16 code-work tasks that declare no `required_secrets` at all; only 6 declare `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`. `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md:1286` states the opposite: *"a subprocess … whose env carries exactly the declared names."* Either the code should filter to the declared set, or the design line is wrong.

**2. The stderr tail escapes masking.** On a code-work failure the last 5 stderr lines are posted verbatim into the item's issue comment inside a fenced block (`executor.mjs:389-390`, from `code-work-run.mjs:74,81`). Actions masking applies to the **run log only** — an issue comment goes through the API unmasked. A worker that prints a token into stderr publishes it into a GitHub issue.

## The loop

1. The agent session is started by `engine/scheduler/queue/invoke.mjs`, which reads the endpoint token out of **the executor job's env** (`env[endpoint.tokenEnv]`).

Any member whose live `claudinite-executor.yml` predates the stamping of an invocation endpoint token it now needs. You're right, and that incident changes my answer. #1296 is exactly the case: `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` **was** set on `hitbut`, but the executor workflow didn't pass it, and because `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot write, the member wedged permanently — the only thing that could deliver the workflow that stamps the token needed the token to run.

So the naming isn't just verbose. **The per-secret naming is what makes the executor workflow change every time a secret arrives, and that file is the one file that cannot converge.** That's the root of the deadlock class, not a side effect of it.

### There is a way to pass all, and it dissolves that half of #1296

`${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` expands the entire `secrets` context into one variable. (`secrets: inherit` does not help — it only works on a reusable-workflow call, and the callee still names each one; `chrome-extension-publish-store.yml:57-61` is that shape in this repo.)

Stamped once as a static line:

```yaml
CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
```

the executor workflow **never needs stamping again**. `withDeclaredSecrets`, the `# claudinite:secrets` marker, and every future withheld `claudinite-executor.yml` caused by a new endpoint token all go away. A member that configures a new endpoint tomorrow works tonight, with no human-merged PR in that repo.

And it lets the design's own claim finally become true rather than aspirational: the executor parses the blob, and hands each task's code-work **only the names it declared** (`required_secrets`), instead of today's `{ ...process.env }` spread at `code-work-run.mjs:67`, which currently gives all three secrets to all ~22 code-work tasks though only 6 declare one. `invoke.mjs:105` reads its endpoint token from the same parsed object. `missingSecrets` keeps working — it just tests the parsed bag instead of `process.env`, and can then finally distinguish "the repo has no such secret" from "the workflow didn't pass it", which is the second half of #1296's diagnosis complaint.

The costs, stated plainly: every repo secret (the `CHROME_*` set here) reaches the executor **job's** env, though not any task's subprocess if we filter as above; and masking is registered per exact literal, so a secret containing `"`, `\` or a newline appears JSON-escaped in the blob and would not be masked if something printed it. Our tokens are `ghp_`/base64url-shaped, so that's theoretical here — but it's the real argument against `toJSON`, and I could not confirm it this session because `docs.github.com` is blocked domain-wide by the egress proxy (`EGRESS_BLOCKED`).

### The stderr-tail claim — no, I can't prove it

Fair challenge. I have **not** seen it happen, and I have no documentation to cite: the same egress block stopped me reaching GitHub's masking docs, and per the pack rule I didn't work down alternate sources for the same denial. What I have is structural only — masking is a filter on the runner's log stream, and `executor.mjs:389-390` sends the tail through the API into an issue body, which doesn't pass through that filter. I'm confident in that mechanism but it is unverified, the trigger requires one of our own workers to print a secret to stderr, and there's no observed instance. Treat it as a note, not a finding; I'd leave the code alone.

input.body:
Sub-issue of #1296, addressing its stamping half.

## The problem

`.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` names every secret it passes, and the wiring converge regenerates that list from `required_secrets` plus configured endpoint tokens (`converge-wiring.mjs:106-117`). That makes the file's content a function of the task set — and it is the one file a converge **cannot write**, because Actions refuses the `GITHUB_TOKEN` under `.github/workflows/` and the refusal rejects the whole ref.

So every new secret or endpoint token needs a human-merged PR in every member. #1296 is what that costs: `hitbut` had `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` set the whole time, but its live executor workflow predated the stamping, the agent could not start, and the only lane that delivers a staged workflow is the agentic apply stage the agent was needed for. Permanently wedged.

## The change

Actions has exactly one way to pass all of them: `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}`, which expands the whole `secrets` context into one variable. (`secrets: inherit` does not help — it is reusable-workflow-call only, and the callee still names each one.)

The executor step carries one static line:

```yaml
CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
```

and the workflow stops being a function of the task set. Nothing about secrets can wedge a member's workflow delivery again.

The executor then parses that bag and, per task, hands code-work **only the names that task declared**. That is a tightening, not a loosening: today `code-work-run.mjs:67` spreads the executor's whole `process.env` into the child, so all three stamped secrets reach the work step of every code-work task though only 6 of ~22 declare one — contradicting `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md:1286` ("whose env carries exactly the declared names"). Parsing a bag is what makes that line true.

`invoke.mjs` reads its endpoint token from the same bag, and its error message can finally distinguish the two causes #1296 says it conflates.

## Compatibility

Fielded members keep an old executor workflow that stamps names directly and sets no `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS`, and that file moves only by human-merged PR — so the reader accepts both: the bag when present, `process.env[NAME]` when it is not. Retirement is gated on no member still running a stamping executor workflow, never a date.

## Known cost

Every repo secret reaches the executor **job**'s env (not any task subprocess, which is filtered). And masking is registered per exact literal, so a secret containing `"`, `\` or a newline appears JSON-escaped in the bag and would not be masked if something printed it — theoretical for token-shaped values, but real. Recorded here rather than discovered later.

{"id":5227778818,"number":1296,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"Withheld-workflow deadlock: a member whose endpoint token is not yet stamped can never deliver the workflow that would stamp it","body":"Confirmed on `missingbulb/hitbut` (missingbulb/hitbut#102), stuck since 2026-08-21.

## The loop

1. The agent session is started by `engine/scheduler/queue/invoke.mjs`, which reads the endpoint token out of **the executor job's env** (`env[endpoint.tokenEnv]`).
2. That variable reaches the job only from `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`, stamped below the `# claudinite:secrets` marker by the wiring converge.
3. The converge **cannot write** `.github/workflows/` — the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` is refused there, and the refusal rejects the whole ref — so `updates/pack-update.mjs` withholds the file into `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`.
4. The **only** thing that delivers a staged workflow is the agentic apply stage, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.md`. Nothing in `engine/` or `updates/` moves it — I grepped every consumer of `PENDING_DIR`.
5. The agent cannot start, because of (1).

So a member that reaches step 3 with an **unstamped** token can never reach step 4. It is not slow, it is not retrying — it is permanently wedged, and no converge, no wake, no force, and no `fleet-baseline` can move it. Only a credential that may write `.github/workflows/` — a human push or a human-merged PR — breaks it.

## Who is exposed

Any member whose live `claudinite-executor.yml` predates the stamping of an invocation endpoint token it now needs. That is not a one-off: it is the ordinary state of every member between "the endpoint gets configured" and "the next apply stage delivers the workflow" — and the deadlock is precisely that the second never happens if the first is what the agent needed.

On `hitbut` the correct file has been sitting in `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` with the right line in it the whole time.

## It is also undiagnosable as written

`invoke.mjs:105-110` observes an empty env var and reports:

> the Actions secret `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` for invocation endpoint "default" is not set in this repo

That asserts a cause the code cannot see. The secret was set the whole time; the workflow simply never passed it. I read the message, believed it, and filed the wrong fix — the owner caught it. Anyone reading that message goes to the Secrets page, sees the secret present, and has nowhere to go next.

The message should say what was observed and name both causes, e.g.:

> `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` is empty in this job. Either the repository secret is not set, **or** `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` does not pass it — check for an undelivered `.claudinite/pending-workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`, which is the usual cause.

## Worth deciding

- **Break the loop in code.** The staged→live move is a file rename with no judgment in it; the reason it is agentic is the *credential*, not the decision. Is there a lane that can deliver it without an agent — the maintenance PR itself carrying the move, for a human to merge, so the deadlock degrades to "waiting on a human" instead of "wedged forever"?
- **Detect it.** A member with a non-empty `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` that has not shrunk in N days is a wedged member by definition. `fleet-roster` already reads member trees; this is one existence check away and would have caught `hitbut` on day one.
- **Fix the message** at `invoke.mjs:110` regardless — it is cheap and it is what cost the diagnosis.

Closes #1301 ## Why The executor workflow named every secret it passed, and the wiring converge regenerated that list from `required_secrets` plus configured endpoint tokens. That made the file's content a function of the task set — and `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot write, so every new secret cost a human-merged PR in every member. #1296 is what that cost in practice: `hitbut` had `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` set the whole time, its live executor workflow predated the stamping, the agent could not start, and the only lane that delivers a staged workflow is the agentic apply stage the agent was needed for. Permanently wedged, with the correct file sitting in `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` the entire time. ## What changed `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` is the only thing Actions offers that passes all of them (`secrets: inherit` is reusable-workflow-call only, and the callee still names each one). The executor step now carries one static line: ```yaml CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} ``` so the workflow no longer tracks declarations at all, and nothing about a secret can wedge workflow delivery again. The selection moves inward, which **tightens** it rather than loosening it. `code-work-run.mjs` used to spread the executor's whole `process.env` into the child, so every code-work task saw every stamped secret though only 6 of 22 declare one. It now gets exactly the names its own declaration lists — which is what `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §14.4 has always claimed. `invoke.mjs` reads its endpoint token from the same bag, and its "missing token" message no longer asserts a cause the code cannot observe — the specific complaint #1296 raised. ## Compatibility A member's live executor workflow moves only by human-merged PR, so `secretValue` falls back to the plain environment when no bag is present. A new rehearsal fixture (`stamping-executor`) holds exactly that shape. Retiring the fallback is gated on no member still stamping — a converge-confirmable condition, not a date. ## Known cost, recorded rather than rediscovered Every repo secret reaches the executor **job**'s env (no task subprocess sees more than it declared). And masking is registered per exact literal, so a secret containing `"`, `\` or a newline appears JSON-escaped in the bag and would not be masked if something printed it — theoretical for token-shaped values, but real, and now stated in DESIGN §14. I could not verify these platform behaviours against GitHub's docs in-session: `docs.github.com` is blocked domain-wide by the sandbox egress proxy. The `toJSON` masking caveat in particular is worth one confirmation from an unblocked environment. ## Folders touched
**`engine/scheduler/queue/`** — new `secrets-bag.mjs`, the only reader of the bag, with the legacy fallback and its retirement condition. `code-work-run.mjs` gains `taskEnv`, which subtracts every secret from the inherited environment and adds back only the declared ones. `invoke.mjs` reads its endpoint token through the bag and reports both causes when it is empty. **`engine/scheduler/`** — `converge-wiring.mjs` loses `declaredSecrets`, `withDeclaredSecrets` and the `# claudinite:secrets` marker; a workflow is now a pure function of its stub. `stubs/claudinite-executor.yml` carries the static line. **`.github/workflows/`** — the canon's own executor copy, edited in the same commit as the stub and diffed against it. **`updates/`** — `pack-update.mjs` withholds the executor stub verbatim instead of computing content from the task set; `engine-update.mjs` follows the changed `convergeWiring` signature. **`vendoring/rehearsal/`** — a `stamping-executor` fixture: a member still passing secrets by name, proving that shape converges green. **`docs/`** — `tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §14 and §12, `task-code-work/DESIGN.md` §9 restated to the mechanism as it now works, with the cost of passing the whole context written down. **`packs/claudinite-growth/`** — `writing-tasks` skill restated to match; version bumped with its `VERSIONS.md` row.
Full suite green (2717 tests), `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking (77 advisory, one fewer than `main`), vendoring rehearsal green across all 25 fixtures. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Answering the original three questions, now with the code behind them:

- **When the inner job uses them?** This was the real finding, and it went the opposite way from what the design claimed: every task's code-work inherited all three secrets. It now gets exactly what its own `required_secrets` lists.

The compatibility half is what protects the case you raised — a member's live workflow still stamping by name resolves from the plain environment, with a rehearsal fixture holding that shape and the retirement gated on "no member still stamps", not a date.

points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
